turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung asked O-lan to rest now and not talk anymore, he would take care of everything and make sure their son was provided for.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung with a determined gaze and told him that she would not rest until their son's marriage was settled and his future secured.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he understood her wishes and would find a suitable wife for him soon, not to worry about his future.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that the eldest son must not be married off hastily, that he was still young and needed time to learn the ways of the world.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son to promise her that he would find a wife who was strong and capable, like she had been, to help him with his household and children.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told Wang Lung that he would choose a wife carefully, with his father's guidance, and that he was eager to learn and become a good husband.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung asked O-lan to calm herself and not worry about the future, that he and their son would see to everything

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was not asking him to promise anything, but to take care of their son and make sure he marries a good woman, for her sake and for their family's future

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan to stop exhausting herself with worry, that he had taken care of their family for many years and would continue to do so after she was gone.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if he had given thought to the future, to their son's children and grandchildren, and if he knew what would become of them after she was gone

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that the future would be taken care of, that the land would provide for their son and his family, and that O-lan should focus on her own recovery.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his father that he would do his best to marry well and bring honor to the family, and that he would follow his father's guidance in all things.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son what kind of woman he thought he would marry, and what qualities he would look for in a wife.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son told his mother that he would be happy to settle down and marry a good woman as soon as his father gave him permission

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was glad the eldest son was thinking of the future, but that she worried still about their son's marriage and who would provide for his children when she was gone

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid suggested that perhaps it would be best to have the eldest son meet with the matchmaker soon, so that his mother's worries could be put to rest

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan must not worry about their son's marriage, that it would all be settled soon and that he would take care of everything.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that the matchmaker had spoken highly of the daughter of the wealthy merchant, and that perhaps their son would be pleased with her

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that the matchmaker's suggestion was a good one and that he would arrange for his son to meet with her at once, so that the marriage could be settled without further delay.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son told his mother that he trusted his father's judgment and was sure that the matchmaker's suggestion would bring them good fortune

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
